Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week — Northbridge's legal team is reviewing Redwood's standard US privacy addendum and we have a couple of open items before we can finalize:

1) Operator vs Service Provider: the current draft labels Redwood as a "Service Provider" under CPRA, but our counsel wants clarity about telemetry and aggregated analytics that we send to you for monitoring. Do you treat telemetry as strictly service-provider processing (no "sale" or use for own purposes)?

2) Subprocessors: please confirm the current subprocessors list, any planned onboarding in the next 90 days, and whether any subprocessors will process data outside the US.

3) Interstate transfers & fallback: we need a contractual onshore fallback guarantee in case offshore subprocessors are unavailable for an incident remediation. Is that something Redwood accepts in the addendum?

Can you provide written confirmation and any evidence (SOC2, subprocessor list) we can attach to our procurement packet?

If helpful, I can share a short redline from our counsel — otherwise we'd appreciate your proposed contract language.

Thanks,

Emma White

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I'll pull in internal owners for details: 

1) Telemetry & "use": Redwood processes telemetry and infrastructure metrics solely to provide and improve the service. We do not "sell" telemetry or use it for targeted advertising. We can add a CPRA-friendly clause: "Redwood will not retain, use, or disclose telemetry for purposes unrelated to performance, security, or service improvement, and will not sell personal information."

2) Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessors CSV and the SOC2 report link. We update the list on a rolling basis and provide 30-days notice for new subprocessors per the addendum; we can commit to 14-days notice for subprocessors that will process data outside the US.

3) Onshore fallback: we do offer an onshore remediation path backed by dedicated capacity in US regions. I am copying Marissa (privacy/product) and Aditya (security/infra) to confirm the exact fallback SLA and provide proposed wording.

I'll follow up with a redline to your DPA and a DocuSign-ready addendum this afternoon.

Best,

Lukas — quick notes from privacy and compliance: 

- "No sale" telemetry language: yes, we can accept the proposed clause. Add a definitional sentence for telemetry to avoid ambiguity: "Telemetry" means non-content logs, metrics, and aggregated performance data provided by Customer or generated by Redwood in the course of providing the service, excluding end-user content.

- Subprocessors list: confirmed attached (subprocessors_list_2026.csv). Planned onboarding: vendor "EdgeStream Ops" is scheduled for limited EU/US support next quarter (not yet processing customer data). No planned offshore changes in the next 90 days that would affect US customers.

- Onshore fallback: Product and Ops can commit to an onshore remediation lane for critical incident response. Proposed contractual language: "If an offshore subprocessor is unavailable for incident remediation, Redwood will activate an onshore remediation path within 8 hours and perform remediation from US-based infrastructure until the offshore subprocessors are restored. Redwood will not pass incremental pass-through costs to Customer for the initial 72 hours of remediation."

- Evidence: attaching SOC2 report (redacted) and our third-party attestation cover letter. Recommend we include both with the DPA addendum.

Happy to walk Legal through any redline.

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
